title: Care Membrane — CQC/CIW Regulations Data

compliance_requirements: Registration with CQC (England) or CIW (Wales) before providing regulated activities
Annual CQC inspection with ratings: Outstanding, Good, Requires Improvement, Inadequate
CQC Key Lines of Enquiry (KLOEs): Safe, Effective, Caring, Responsive, Well-Led
CIW inspection against National Minimum Standards and outcome-focused frameworks
Data Security and Protection Toolkit (DSPT) annual submission — mandatory for all health and social care organisations with NHS connections
GDPR Article 9 compliance for processing special category health data
Mental Capacity Act 2005 compliance for care decisions
Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 compliance in care settings
Fire safety regulations (Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005) for care homes
Safe staffing levels: NICE guideline (NG120) for safe staffing in care homes
Medication management: NICE guideline (NG5) and CQC Regulation 12 expectations
Clinical governance framework with incident reporting and learning systems
Whistleblowing policy under Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998
AI governance requirements for care homes deploying monitoring/AAL systems — transparency, bias, data minimisation, human oversight per EU AI Act Article 26 (extraterritorial if serving EU residents)
CQC 'Registering the Right Support' framework for learning disability/autism services
Information governance: ICO registration, data breach reporting, subject access request handling
penalties: CQC Enforcement Action: Warning notices, conditions of registration, suspension or cancellation of registration — no upper limit on harm to service users
CQC: Financial penalties up to £1,000,000 per breach under Section 86A of Health and Social Care Act 2008 (as amended by Health and Social Care Act 2022)
Magistrates' Court: Unlimited fine for conviction under Health and Social Care Act 2008
Prohibition orders: Individual managers can be banned from providing or managing care services
CIW: Compliance notices, improvement notices, cancellation of registration
CIW: Financial penalty up to £50,000 per offence under Social Services and Well-being (Wales) Act 2014
ICO enforcement: Up to £17,500,000 or 4% of annual worldwide turnover for GDPR breaches involving care data
Criminal prosecution for corporate manslaughter under Corporate Manslaughter and Corporate Homicide Act 2007 for care home deaths linked to systemic failures
Care provider inclusion on CQC 'special measures' list — publicly available, blocks local authority commissioning
NHS contracting consequences: DSPT breach can result in suspension of NHS data sharing, blocking medication dispensing, GP referrals and A&E admissions
